provenance.method: Pearson chi-square test of independence (Pearson 1900; no Yates continuity correction -- standard practice for r x c tables, applied uniformly here) + Cramer's V = sqrt(chi2/(n*(min(r,c)-1)))

assumptions_checked: Cochran's rule cleared before this test ran (matrix §4a EXIT-07): >= 80% of cells expected >= 5, no cell expected < 1
counts are independent observations (one per unit, not repeated measures)
value.effect_size_ci_method: not computed -- no simple closed-form CI for Cramer's V (a bootstrap or noncentral-chi-square CI is out of scope for this v1 route); the point estimate is reported plainly.

plain_language.comparison_summary: Tested whether the row categories (misshelved, ok) and column categories (adult, juvenile, nonfiction) are associated -- a 2x3 contingency table, n=1379, chi-square test of independence.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Cramer's V = 0.120 -- a weak association between the row and column categories (0 = no association, 1 = perfect association).
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0000, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 0.0048% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.
